request: Extend this local Python inventory tool with a JSON batch-import command. # Supplied discovery

This is a constructed planning fixture. Source, tests and data are present; the baseline suite passed. Only existing behavior was tested. No new feature, atomicity or search acceptance is implied. No earlier decision experiment is supplied.

# Architecture

## Stack

Python standard library; sqlite3 local persistence. No dependencies, server or external service.

## Structure

Existing src/adapter.py exports apply(db_path, rows); tests/test_baseline.py covers its single-row client. data/seed.json is read-only. Planned tests/support.py owns disposable SQL fixtures, subprocess barriers and cleanup (W1). Planned src/_apply_rows.py is an internal adapter-worker entrypoint used only by importer; planned src/__main__.py owns CLI dispatch; src/importer.py owns JSON validation, staging and publication. tests/test_import.py will retain unit/component/CLI checks; these files are not implemented yet.

Python resolves the existing src package from the repository root. New modules use relative imports from . import adapter and from .importer import import_json; stdlib modules use absolute imports. No new top-level module shadows json, sqlite3 or tempfile. The private worker module is invoked with sys.executable -B -m src._apply_rows from the owned package root, stage path argument and validated row JSON on stdin; its accepted result is internal only. importer.import_json(db_path, input_path) is the narrow component seam consumed by CLI and tests; validation and staging helpers remain private. Tests import src inside test methods so unittest discovery can load before the product module exists; RED must assert the missing seam/command as failure, not skip it.

Existing/destination storage remains inventory(sku TEXT PRIMARY KEY, quantity INTEGER), no extra tables, migrations or version markers. JSON values are validated before storage; importer does not retrofit CHECK constraints on existing data. SQLite backup snapshots all existing tables, then installed adapter updates inventory only on that snapshot, preserving unrelated state. A random private stage in the live database's parent is transient, never authoritative. Permissions of an existing live file must be retained; new files use restrictive tempfile permissions. No remote store, retention quota, PII, cache or background jobs are introduced. Process-kill leftovers are ignored, never auto-promoted or glob-deleted; the current invocation cleans only its own known stage paths.

## Conventions

Small explicit functions, unittest, disposable fixtures. Preserve existing public adapter API and baseline. Use descriptive test methods with TC_n first-line docstrings for visible IDs.

## Interfaces and boundaries

Proposed CLI: python3 -B -m src import-json --db DB INPUT; required explicit paths, JSON array of exact sku/quantity objects. Proposed defaults: unique nonempty string SKUs, quantities integer 0..2**63-1 excluding bool, duplicate SKUs rejected, empty batch no-op. Parsing/validation precedes any live-state write; concise nonzero errors, no success before publication. These are implementation defaults, not extra user requirements.

Adapter behavior is observed in RUN/scratch/adapter-probe.json: per-row commit on its own connection survives later failure and external caller rollback. Preserve its implementation and use it only against an isolated stage. A SQLite backup plus same-directory replacement has mechanism evidence in the plan decision note and frozen publication-probe-verified.json. It is selected for ordinary DELETE-journal databases with no live sidecars; implementation and retained acceptance checks are still due. Preflight rejects non-DELETE modes, existing live sidecars and symlinks without repair or mutation. Explicitly close connections; snapshot all tables through SQLite backup rather than raw file copy.

## Real-boundary checks

Every product boundary is local. Owner: implementation for TC_1..TC_10, due at item test and system-test. Definition and exact fixture/oracle are environment.md ## Harnesses and suites. CLI end-to-end procedure: create disposable DB via independent SQL with keep=9,old=2; write [{"sku":"old","quantity":7},{"sku":"new","quantity":4}]; invoke actual command; assert exit 0 and count 2, reopen via sqlite3 and assert sorted full rows [(keep,9),(new,4),(old,7)]. Reinvoke and compare again. This is planned, not executed: CLI absent.

Interruption/recovery procedure TC_4,TC_5,TC_10: create same independent initial state; run separate children with barriers after the first staged adapter commit and immediately before replace; observe barrier and old live rows, send SIGINT and SIGKILL in separate trials, reap, reopen old state; rerun to full new state; run separate post-replace interruption to confirm complete committed new state and safe retry. Interrupted precommit must never expose a prefix. Validate both existing and initially absent destinations. Inject actual rename failure in TC_8. A mocked rename alone cannot prove publication visibility: runtime experiment and postimplementation filesystem checks must exercise os.replace. Filesystem/process checks use actual local SQLite/rename, not a remote or mock persistence claim.

Literal interruption after successful replacement cannot ensure old data: publication is the linearization point, and response delivery can fail afterward. Recovery retries are idempotent. No power-loss guarantee or concurrently open WAL-reader support is inferred from a process-kill test. Sidecar policy is fail-closed preflight: reject live -wal/-shm/-journal or non-DELETE journal mode; never delete or promote them. Product guard checks remain due in TC_8. Local CLI is the consumer surface; browser/device/authentication/remote reconciliation and remote-native tests do not apply to this explicitly local request. No unavailable external boundary is reported as a pass.

## Decisions

AD-1: Preserve supplied standard-library stack, installed adapter and existing baseline; accepted.
AD-2: Direct-live apply and caller-transaction wrapping are rejected: disposable adapter 2.3 probe observes partial commits after invalid-middle input and survival after outer rollback. Retain adapter for rows and isolate writes; staging/publication choice and scoped feasibility evidence are recorded in AD-4.

AD-3: Accepted namespace/placement: W1 tests/support.py reuses unittest/sqlite3/tempfile/subprocess; W2 src/importer.py exposes import_json to src/__main__.py and component tests, with private validation/staging helpers. Existing adapter remains unchanged. Alternatives rejected: generic utility package, new dependency or external service; none has a present consumer.
AD-4: Accepted publication architecture, with mechanism-only local evidence: validate complete JSON, allocate unpredictable private stage next to DB, SQLite backup of existing DB into stage (or initialize stage for a missing DB), explicitly close snapshot handles, apply through adapter.apply(stage, rows) in a short-lived local Python worker, wait for successful process exit, force/verify stage rollback journal mode and closed handles, preserve existing file mode, flush stage, then os.replace(stage, live) once. Never remove live first. Publication success is the replace linearization point; cleanup/report errors after that point cannot turn committed state into an uncommitted failure. Current cleanup is best effort and narrowly owned. Evidence rejects live application and caller wrapping (AD-2). A2/E1 publication-probe-verified.json observes private prefix/full staging, live old before replace, full new afterward, SIGINT/SIGKILL interruption, real rename error and idempotent retry, preserved metadata and absent-target behavior. Preflight must reject active live -wal/-shm/-journal, non-DELETE live journal mode and symlinks; do not auto-delete or normalize live files. Actual guard behavior is due implementation TC_8. No other filesystem, long-lived WAL reader, concurrent writer or power-loss guarantee is inferred.
AD-5: Accepted data/default policy: preserve existing SQLite table and unrelated tables/rows; replace quantities, do not accumulate. Require exact JSON sku/quantity fields, nonblank string SKU, unique SKU per batch, integer quantity 0..2**63-1 excluding bool. Empty batch is a successful no-op, including no destination creation. Reject source/destination alias before mutation. Source retained seed is never a probe destination. No schema migration is needed; existing nullable schema is preserved, validation belongs at new input boundary.
AD-6: Accepted interaction: operator -> local CLI arguments + JSON file -> synchronous importer -> installed row adapter on private snapshot -> atomic live publication -> JSON success count. Error goes to stderr/nonzero, with no success before commit. No server/queue/cache/async acknowledgement; no accepted-but-unprocessed state. SIGINT/SIGKILL before commit keeps old visible inventory; termination after commit yields complete new inventory with acknowledgement uncertainty and safe repeat. This linearization caveat is a disclosed necessary limit on the literal interruption wording, not an execution pass. Documentation must explain it. Remote delivery, visual styling/motion/accessibility and external identity are outside CLI scope.

AD-7: Accepted adapter handle-lifetime boundary: adapter.py has no exposed close handle and sqlite3 connection context exit does not close the connection. Keep installed adapter unchanged, but run row application in private src/_apply_rows.py subprocess; wait/reap successful exit to close all adapter handles before publication. E2 worker-probe.json observes complete/private success, invalid-middle partial stage with exit 1, prefix-interrupted worker exit -9 with old live map, and repeated successful actual replacement. Parent closes its snapshot handles explicitly and owns publication exclusively; worker receives only stage path/validated JSON stdin, no live path. Parent forwards no worker success before publication. Normal error/SIGINT terminates/reaps worker before cleanup; SIGKILL may leave stage-only work, which recovery ignores. No remote worker or model. Alternatives rejected: replacing adapter, relying on GC, patching global sqlite3.connect. Product lifecycle/error protocol and retained tests still due W2.

## Superseded

Synthetic prior summaries and discovery.md are context only. They contain no feature tests or decision experiment. The actual R-1 request governs planning; ignore stray search wording in supplied notes as unrelated.

# Environment

## Targets and runtimes

Local Python 3.9.6 standard library, SQLite through sqlite3; current runner evidence: RUN/scratch/baseline.json (RUN is the active external ShipLoop run directory). All commands start in the owned worktree. No network, dependency download, account or deployment is required or authorized. data/seed.json is retained read-only input. All generated fixtures and captured outputs belong in RUN/scratch or a TemporaryDirectory beneath it; set TMPDIR to RUN/scratch when invoking unittest because the existing test uses tempfile defaults.

## Commands

Existing full suite (discovery includes all test_*.py), measured under one second with one test; prospective full cost under 30 seconds with bounded subprocess waits. Current observation is one baseline case only, not feature acceptance:

python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
